Before the first step: what a knowledge base needs#

A knowledge base is the one supported area whose prerequisites live outside the base install. The alpha install page's native path has none of them. Check each before you create one, because the failure comes late (a build that stops, not a form that refuses) when one is missing.

NeedWhyIf it is missing
An S3-compatible object store holding the sources (MinIO, or S3)sources are read from a bucket (kind: file or folder in it), and the build writes its chunks and graph backcreating a knowledge base answers 503 and says the object store is unreachable. Set CALIBER_OBJECT_STORE_ENDPOINT_URL and credentials, or use the docker stack, which runs MinIO
pip install "caliber-suite[knowledge,knowledge-local]"the knowledge extra gives chunking and entity extraction; the embedding libraries (sentence-transformers, langchain-huggingface, and torch) are in knowledge-localthe options list every embedding model as unavailable, with a reason that names the extra, and creating fails fast with the same sentence. The default docker image installs knowledge but not knowledge-local: add it through CALIBER_INSTALL_EXTRAS when you build
An embedding model on the hostthe first build downloads the model from Hugging Face (about 90 MB for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, more for the larger ones)an offline host fails at the first build. Pre-cache the model into HF_HOME while online, then build
PostgreSQL with the pgvector extensiononly for ANN search, which is opt-in with CALIBER_KNOWLEDGE_PGVECTOR_ENABLED=true. Without it retrieval scans the stored vectors, which is fine at small scalenothing breaks; large corpora get slower
Apache AGEonly for the graph retrieval mode age_graph. Optionalthat mode is not offered, and the other modes work

CALIBER_ALLOW_FLAGGED_LOCAL_EMBEDDINGS=true is a different thing: it lets embeddings run on an install whose torch version is on the advisory list. It cannot install a missing package, so a missing package is never reported as something an override fixes.

What is verified, and what is not#

tests/test_knowledge_stack_journey.py runs create, build, version, query, activate and roll back against the docker stack's real MinIO and PostgreSQL (scripts/verify-knowledge-stack.sh; the stack-smoke workflow runs it weekly and on pull requests that touch deploy/, the stack scripts or caliber/src/caliber/knowledge/, and it is not a required check on every pull request). Its embeddings are simulated: a deterministic bag-of-words double stands in for a model, so a green run shows the storage, the build and the routes work on the real services and says nothing about retrieval quality. Judge quality with your own model and test set.

Who can do what#

Inside a project, creating, changing or deleting a knowledge base, building a version, activating or rolling back a version, syncing a version to Apache AGE and setting a baseline need editor or owner. Running a calibration needs reviewer, editor or owner. Listing, reading and querying need only membership. A member whose role is too weak gets 403 and a person outside the project gets 404. Calibrating a knowledge base returns a run summary and has no candidate to apply.

1. What knowledge bases are for in CALIBER#

Knowledge bases give CALIBER a governed retrieval surface: versioned corpora, ingestion, chunking, embeddings, optional graph extraction, and retrieval that can be measured rather than assumed.
